Thanks Anna — sketch received, helpful. Answers inline and a short tech checklist to make the spike productive.

On storing embeddings
- For the pilot I recommend Pinecone (managed, lowest ops). ES can work but requires mapping tuning and more ops to scale; costs will be higher if you host. We can also prototype with a small in-memory FAISS in the sample app for functional testing.

Local SDK quickstart checklist (Python + TypeScript)
1) Environment
  - Python 3.10+ virtualenv or Poetry.
  - Node 18+ and yarn/npm.
  - Git clone sample repo: https://github.com/redwoodinference/bridge-pilot-samples (we’ll populate before the spike).

2) Auth options
  - Dev: API key in .env (REDWOOD_API_KEY).
  - Staging/prod: OIDC via your Okta tenant — we’ll provide an OIDC sample config (auth-config-examples.md attached).

3) SDK install & basic usage
  - Python: pip install redwood-sdk
  - TS: npm install @redwoodinference/sdk
  - Basic pattern: create client -> route request to embedding model -> store embeddings -> rerank by score -> call structured tool for follow-up.

4) Routing & model selection
  - Use our SDK route config to prefer smaller embedding models for bulk indexing (cost) and route to larger reranker/generation models for scoring.
  - We’ll include a sample route policy in the repo (routes.json).

5) Structured output & tool calling example
  - Provide a simple tool contract: {"open_ticket": {"fields": ["summary","priority","customer_id"]}}
  - Demo will show a tool call from the model that returns a JSON payload we can forward to your ticketing API.

6) Reranker notes
  - We’ll ship a baseline TF-IDF + semantic reranker pipeline. For pilot evals we’ll run a small MRR test set and share results.

Attachments I’m adding to this thread: sdk-setup-commands.sh (smoke commands you can run locally), auth-config-examples.md (Okta OIDC samples).

If you can confirm the S3 object path and give a temporary API key for the dev sandbox, I’ll stage a small dataset and push the sample repo updates tonight.
